verdict.rationale: Proa documents async renderers, loader caching through WebContext, and Suspense streaming for slow data. It also documents hydrated islands that emit server-rendered HTML plus JS with per-island seed state, so async server data feeding interactive components is strongly implied. However, the explicit handoff of fetched data from an async server component into an island's props is never shown. Missing for 10: a documented example of async data fetching passed as props or seed state into an interactive island, details of serialization across the server/client boundary, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can fetch data in asynchronous server-rendered components and pass it down to interactive client components

citations.quote: Every render has typed access to request-scoped data, response metadata, route state, and loader caching through the same WebContext
let Suspense boundaries stream ready chunks out of order when slow data should not block the page
Add signals and event handlers, and Proa emits the server-rendered HTML plus the JavaScript required for that island
Each hydrated RSJS island emits a small vanilla-JS module plus seed state
